What We Build

One company.
One way of building products.

Antutive exists to create products, not projects. Three principles decide what we take on and how we build it.

AI-native by design

We build products where the intelligence is the product, not a feature bolted on afterwards. If the AI came out and the product still worked, we'd build something else.

Products that carry real work

We start from problems people actually live with — the everyday coordination, interpretation and follow-through that today's software leaves to humans.

Built and operated, not handed over

Antutive designs, builds and runs its own products for the long term. Owning the product end-to-end is the company's model — not client delivery.

Products

A portfolio that grows
only when something is real.

Antutive is structured to create and operate multiple products over time. Products appear here when they exist — never before.

Our product philosophy
Product Spotlight · Famant

The first product from Antutive.

Famant is an AI-powered family management and household coordination platform: one shared context for a family's schedules, tasks and documents, with an assistant that proposes actions and acts on your confirmation.

Famant is the flagship product of Antutive (ANTUTIVE AB), built and operated in Gothenburg, Sweden. Famant is in development and pre-launch — capabilities carry honest status labels, and real screenshots and a recorded demo will be published as they become real.

How We Build

Mechanism-first,
confirmation-first.

Every Antutive product is designed as model-driven behaviour with a human in the loop: the intelligence reads, reasons and proposes — the person confirms before anything happens. And we describe our products in mechanisms and honest statuses, never in adjectives.

We're finalising our cloud and model architecture and will publish it on the technology page as it's confirmed. We publish measured results only once we've measured them.

Read about our technology

One flow from Famant, end to end

  1. 1

    Input

    You photograph a birthday invitation.

  2. 2

    Understanding

    The assistant is designed to read it — date, time, place, child.

  3. 3

    Proposal

    It proposes the calendar event, a gift reminder and an RSVP task.

  4. 4

    Confirmation

    Nothing is added until a family member confirms.
